correctness.rationale: For all n>=3, the exterior-neighbor equations t-1_{i in T} and s-1_{j in S} reduce every fort to the three listed inclusion-minimal families. The standard fort-transversal equivalence yields all zero forcing sets and the exact polynomial. Summing triple inequalities and checking the uniform 1/3 vector proves Z*=2n/3 and unique optimality for n>=4. Matching explicit disjoint forts in all residue classes proves ft=floor(2n/3), and the integer zero-forcing formula and limit follow. Independent original-graph exhaustive checks and LP/packing tests corroborate but are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The result specifies the entire obstruction hypergraph and all successful initial sets, not merely a small parameter value. It settles the complete zero-forcing polynomial, exact integral and fractional optima, disjoint-fort packing, and fractional rigidity for an infinite, natural dense bipartite family. It shows deleting a perfect matching changes fractional zero forcing by n/3 but integral zero forcing by only 2, producing an exact asymptotic threefold LP gap instead of the complete-bipartite twofold gap; the phenomenon is mathematically motivated by fort-transversal methods.
